All 16 tests pass, confirming the plugin extension and the decoupled scaffold logic are correct.

## Summary

**`plugins/pantoken/custom-theme-colors/src/index.ts`** — extended `customThemeColorsCss()`/`customThemeColors()` with two new options instead of a workaround:
- `selector` — scopes the conditional `[data-pantoken-color="…"]` rules to something other than `:root`, so two independently-themed instances can coexist on one page.
- `resetSelector` — emits one unconditional rule pinning every token the plugin can touch back to its own true base value, so a subtree (e.g. a color-swatch legend) stays constant regardless of an ancestor's active color scope.

Added 3 new tests covering both options (16/16 passing).

**`packages/scaffold/templates/canvas-theme-editor/src/main.ts.tmpl`** — redid the chrome/preview decoupling (lost to a concurrent commit) and applied the new plugin option:
- Chrome (toolbar/buttons outside the tray) now swaps its own theme-variant stylesheet and color via `applyChromeTheme`/`applyChromeColor`, driven only by the docs page's `postMessage` broadcasts.
- The tray's theme/color buttons and the TinyMCE editor skin are driven only by local tray state (`selectedTheme`/`selectedColor`); docs broadcasts no longer touch them, and tray clicks no longer touch the chrome's `data-pantoken-color`.
- `customThemeColorsCss(undefined, { resetSelector: "#theme-tray" })` pins the tray's own subtree (its buttons and the 13 reference swatches) to true, unremapped colors, so they no longer visually shift to match the chrome's active color.
